title: Inpatient operations and throughput
scenario: A hospital asks whether one department has deteriorating throughput. Analyse 90-day encounter volume, mean/median LOS, discharge destination and supplied readmission flags by department and month.
approach: Define encounter grain; validate date range and LOS; stratify by department and month; show counts and uncertainty; investigate case-mix; write a one-page executive summary.
deliverables: Encounter-level monthly KPI table; dashboard wireframe; 5-slide narrative; limitations register.
guardrails: Do not label association as performance causation; supplied readmission flags are not validated outcomes.

title: Antihypertensive drug utilisation evaluation
scenario: A tertiary-care pharmacy team wants a synthetic DUE review of antihypertensive prescribing, combinations, comorbidities and BP documentation.
approach: Define inclusion/exclusion; map generic names/classes; assess monotherapy/combination patterns; check dose/route/frequency completeness; summarise baseline/follow-up BP; separate prescribing indicators from clinical outcomes.
deliverables: DUE protocol; cleaned synthetic dataset; prescribing indicator table; 2-page clinical interpretation.
guardrails: Order records do not prove administration/adherence; do not infer guideline concordance without patient-specific context and dated guideline.

title: Pharmacovigilance signal triage
scenario: Safety team receives spontaneous case reports and requests a screening-priority summary.
approach: Deduplicate case IDs; classify seriousness separately from severity; inspect missingness and chronology; compute descriptive counts and disproportionality screening only when comparator data are valid.
deliverables: Case reconciliation log; signal-screening table; narrative triage memo.
guardrails: ROR/PRR are screening measures, not causality; no regulatory conclusion from synthetic reports.

title: Claims-based adherence proxy
scenario: Payer asks for a descriptive antihypertensive medication availability measure.
approach: Define eligible continuous enrolment; construct days-supply coverage; define refill overlap and allowable gap; compute PDC; conduct sensitivity analyses.
deliverables: Cohort flow; PDC distribution; exclusions; sensitivity table.
guardrails: Claims-based possession is not ingestion; days supply assumptions and enrollment completeness matter.

title: Real-world evidence cohort design
scenario: Research team wants to compare two treatment initiation cohorts using observational data.
approach: Specify target population, new-user design, index date, baseline lookback, follow-up, outcomes, censoring and confounders; create a DAG; assess positivity and balance.
deliverables: Protocol synopsis; cohort specification; baseline table; analysis plan.
guardrails: Propensity score adjustment does not remove unmeasured confounding; avoid causal wording without assumptions.

title: Clinical trial data quality
scenario: A study manager reports inconsistent dates, duplicate subjects and out-of-range observations.
approach: Check subject uniqueness, visit windows, missingness, range checks, cross-field logic and query ageing; distinguish source correction from derived correction.
deliverables: Data-cleaning plan; issue log; query metrics; reproducible QC script.
guardrails: Never silently overwrite source values; maintain audit trail and protocol context.

title: Emergency department flow
scenario: ED leadership wants to understand arrival-to-provider and arrival-to-disposition delays.
approach: Validate timestamp ordering/time zones; calculate intervals; stratify by triage acuity and shift; report median and upper quantiles; identify missing timestamps.
deliverables: Metric dictionary; timestamp QC report; flow dashboard concept.
guardrails: Do not rank teams without case-mix and timestamp completeness assessment.

title: Laboratory turnaround time
scenario: Lab director wants order-to-collection, collection-to-result and total turnaround by test and priority.
approach: Define timestamp events; remove/flag impossible sequences; separate cancelled tests; calculate median and 90th percentile; stratify by priority.
deliverables: TAT metric table; exception report; operational recommendations.
guardrails: A result timestamp is not equivalent to clinician acknowledgement or treatment.
